title: Local vs Global vs Server State: Key Idea

scenes.line1: Why split state into local, global, and server?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why React apps talk about local, global, and server state? Let’s clear up when each one matters most.

scenes.label: Local
scenes.sub: State inside one component, like a text input value.
scenes.say: Local state lives inside a single component. Think of a form input or a toggle switch. No one else needs to know about it.

scenes.label: Global
scenes.sub: State shared by many components, like user info.
scenes.say: Global state is for data many components need, like the logged-in user or the app’s theme.

scenes.label: Server
scenes.sub: Data fetched from APIs, needs syncing and caching.
scenes.say: Server state comes from APIs. It changes outside your app, so you need to fetch and sync it.
Redux and Context help with global state. React Query or SWR handle server state, with caching and refetching built in.

scenes.question: Should you use Redux for all state?
scenes.right: No. Use local state for isolated data, Redux for shared client state, and React Query for server data.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: should you use Redux for everything? Nope. Use local state where possible, Redux for shared client data, and React Query for anything from the server.
